subject: Post-demo model recommendations & decision criteria for FinPilot POC
messages:
From: Liam O'Connell <liam@finpilot.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Nora Chen <nora@finpilot.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: demo & request for model shortlist + cost/latency tradeoffs

Thanks again for the demo today — it was helpful. A few follow-ups from our side as we align the POC team: 

1) Can you send a concise recommended shortlist (2-4 models) for our use case (customer-facing summarization + entity extraction at ~1k tokens per request, 200 qps target) with the tradeoffs (cost, typical p50/p99 latency on your hosted stack, quality notes and any known regression risks)?
2) We want any benchmark links and the exact prompt set you used for the quick demo so our ML infra can reproduce locally.
3) Do you have guidance on expected unit economics if we push to dedicated capacity during the POC (approx 40M tokens/month)?

Constraints: low tail latency matters (p99 < 500ms for apdex), occasional long context up to 4k tokens (but rare). Data residency: US only.

Appreciate a short prioritized recommendation (we want to present to our CTO tomorrow).

--
Liam O'Connell
Product Lead, FinPilot
liam@finpilot.com
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connell <liam@finpilot.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Nora Chen <nora@finpilot.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: demo & request for model shortlist + cost/latency tradeoffs

Liam — thanks for the clear asks. Below is a compact, prioritized shortlist and the rationale tailored to the FinPilot constraints (200 qps target, p99 sensitivity, occasional 4k tokens). I attached the prompt set we used (finpilot-eval-prompt-set-v1.jsonl) and our benchmark export (fp-benchmarks-20270420.csv). Also linking the runbook exec summary for ops considerations.

Executive shortlist (recommended order):

1) redwood/phoenix-13B-int8 (recommended default)
   - Rationale: Best balance of cost, p50/p99 latency, and quality on summarization + structured entity extraction.
   - Latency (hosted, m5 GPU profile): p50 ~ 110ms, p95 ~ 260ms, p99 ~ 420ms for 1k-token requests; 4k token tail extends p99 to ~980ms but rare.
   - Quality: Matches 70-80% of larger 70B quality on extraction precision; excellent summarization coherence in our prompt set.
   - Cost estimate (hosted): ~$0.065 per 1k input+output tokens. Dedicated reserved pricing could reduce unit cost to ~$0.035–0.045 per 1k at 40M tokens/mo depending on commitment.
   - Ops: Recommended quantized int8 variant for most requests; enable KV cache for sessions with multi-turn context.

2) redwood/tenor-7B-q4 (low-cost fallback)
   - Rationale: If cost-first or high concurrency required, this model serves as a fast fallback with good latency and acceptable extraction recall.
   - Latency: p50 ~ 55ms, p95 ~ 140ms, p99 ~ 300ms (1k tokens).
   - Quality: Slightly lower extraction precision vs phoenix-13B, requires prompt tuning on edge cases.
   - Cost: ~$0.025 per 1k tokens hosted; dedicated ~ $0.015–0.022 per 1k.
   - Use-case: Bulk/ingest paths, optimistic cache hits, or initial pass before heavier rerank/extraction with phoenix-13B.

3) redwood/atlas-70B-int8 (quality-first for critical flows)
   - Rationale: Best-in-class quality for nuanced summarization and entity disambiguation; useful for high-value workflows where correctness matters more than cost.
   - Latency: p50 ~ 240ms, p95 ~ 520ms, p99 ~ 980ms (1k tokens) — higher for 4k.
   - Cost: ~$0.45 per 1k tokens hosted; dedicated pricing and quantization can lower this to ~$0.22–0.30 per 1k with reserved capacity.
   - Ops: Recommend canarying on small subset of users and automatic fallback to phoenix-13B on p99 threshold breaches.

Quality/regression notes and guardrails:
- We ran the attached prompt set against the three models and the CSV includes per-prompt F1/exact-match metrics. Phoenix-13B consistently reduces spurious entity hallucinations vs tenzor-7B when prompts include explicit schema constraints.
- Atlas-70B shows occasional verbosity drift; if you adopt it, we recommend a short regression harness (we can onboard your example set) and monitoring alerting on a small set of golden prompts.
- Recommend threshold-based rollout: start with phoenix-13B as default, route 10% of traffic to atlas-70B for gold paths, and use tenzor-7B for batch/low-latency passes.

Next steps I suggest (short):
- We drop the attached prompt pack into your infra and you reproduce the CSV locally (link to Drive below).
- Redwood provides a 7-day dedicated eval window (subject to approval) for the phoenix-13B int8 profile — Ben to confirm commercial terms.
- We'll draft a short mutual action plan and a minimal eval acceptance criteria doc (precision/latency SLOs).

Attachments: finpilot-eval-prompt-set-v1.jsonl (prompt fixtures); fp-benchmarks-20270420.csv (raw metrics); redwood-model-runbook-exec-summary.pdf (ops checklist).

Links: https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/finpilot/20270420 (detailed charts)

Happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up today if you want to walk the metrics.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
